And the armies of the Huns and of the Slavs spent the night and encamped against the royal city,
and they breached the outer wall,
and plundered and burned all the suburbs,
and took captive all they could find, and departed.
And they came again a second and a third time.
And then the Romans took courage,
and destroyed them in battle;
and the few of them who escaped {OCR?}
were never seen again anywhere.
After Justinian, Justin the Third (the Second?), thirteen years.
This man was the nephew (sister's son) of the one before him,
and was Thracian by race.
He reigned together with Sophia, his wife, in the latter Tishrin (November),
and there was absolutely no oppression in his days,
and evildoers ceased because of his strength.
His feet, however, were diseased.
And at that time, there was Khosrow, king of the Persians.
And at first they were at peace,
so that Justin even sent gifts of honor in his second year to Khosrow,
by the hands of John the patrician of Callinicum.
When, however, the Persians began to compel the Armenians to worship fire like the Magians,
the Armenians rebelled against the Persians
and took refuge with the Romans.
And thus the peace was broken.
Khosrow sent to Justin:
"It is not right that you should lend a hand to a people who have rebelled against their king.
And if you accept the people,
their land is mine;
let them depart from my land."
Justin answered:
"A Christian people who have fled from the worship of demons and taken refuge with me,
I will not deliver into your hands.
And since they have become mine,
their land has also become mine with them."
Khosrow, however, wrote a second time:
"If you give neither the people nor the land,
give the tribute that your kings used to give formerly for Armenia."
Justin replied even more harshly:
"I will even demand back from you the gold that you formerly took;
and how can you demand from us the northern region,
when we even claim Nisibis? Because it belongs to the Romans,
and it was given to the Persians on conditions,
as is written in the archives."
And in his eighth year,
he made Marcian, his maternal aunt's son, Caesar,
and sent him with a Roman army against Nisibis.
